name: qdoc preparation — option 2: one QDoc aggregate with invitations
description: Direction of this option: one consolidated QDoc aggregate root that owns its versions, each version's content files and attachments, comments, per-approver file approvals, reviewed marks, and the version's invitations and assignments of authors, reviewers and approvers. The root checks every drafting invariant synchronously in one transaction: one version in preparation and one published at a time, at least one content file per version, at least one approver before sharing, no open comments and an active file before approval, lock after approval, the version approved the moment the last approver approves the last file, archiving only with no version in force or in preparation, and no assignments or versions once archived. Optimistic concurrency on the whole aggregate, plus a per-file revision so an approver approves exactly the content they saw, handles concurrent editing. People are assigned through invitations as on GitHub: the quality manager (or the auditor on own document) invites a person to a role on a version, the invitee accepts, and all assignment checks run at acceptance; a failed check refuses the assignment. The module tree is shallow under the root qdocmanagement: drafting holds the aggregate and its use cases; numbering the <sequence>/<month>/<year> numbers with organisation prefix and suffix, demo prefix and auditor suffix; scanning the attachment scanner port; activity the audit trail, written in the same transaction as the change; notifications the e-mails. A failed attachment scan removes the file automatically as a system action and e-mails the author. It gains simple, strongly consistent invariant enforcement and few building blocks; it costs a large aggregate, contention when several authors edit at once, and an extra invitation step. Out of scope: late correction between approval and publication (the approval lock is absolute here; deferred to a later change), publication itself (it reaches drafting only as recordPublication and recordWithdrawal), attachment size limits (undecided pending research), tracking attachment downloads, and everything section 10 of the requirements lists: employee sign-off, templates, AI reviewers, other approval strategies, per-section approval and deletion.

description.value: QDoc management: the bounded context for quality documents (procedures, guidelines, instructions, policies) that organisations holding a quality certificate must maintain. This change covers drafting, from creating a QDoc until a version is approved; publication, employee sign-off and deletion live elsewhere or later. The root package also holds the shared notions of users, roles and organisations that every child module relies on.

description.value: The quality document and everything drafted in it, as one aggregate: its versions (entities), each version's content files and attachments (entities), comments, per-approver file approvals, reviewed marks, invitations and assignments. The root checks every invariant synchronously in one transaction. The whole aggregate is saved under optimistic concurrency (concurrencyVersion): two commands that changed the same QDoc from the same starting point cannot both commit; the loser is rejected and retried on fresh state. This makes the invariants simple and strongly consistent, at the cost of a large aggregate and contention when several authors edit at once. Each file additionally carries a revision so an approver approves exactly the content they saw. Every change raises a QDoc event the activity list records.

Each command loads one QDoc, looks up the acting user in the user directory, calls one method of the QDoc root, and saves the aggregate under optimistic concurrency. The QDoc's events go synchronously to the activity list in the same transaction, and after commit to notifications and scanning. A concurrency conflict is answered as such; the client reloads and retries.

description.value:
Creates a QDoc. Input: the acting user and CreateQDoc. Looks up the creator, has the numbering module generate the document number (auditor suffix when the creator is an auditor, demo prefix in a demo instance), calls QDoc.create and saves. Output: the new QDoc's id. Every other quality manager of the organisation is notified after commit.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  Quality manager->>QDocDraftingService: createQDoc(userId, command)
  QDocDraftingService->>UserDirectory: findUser(userId)
  QDocDraftingService->>DocumentNumberGenerator: generate(organisationId, creatorRoles, now)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDoc: create(id, command, number, creator, now)
  QDoc-->>QDocDraftingService: QDocCreated, InvitationSent*
  QDocDraftingService->>QDocRepository: save(qdoc)
  QDocDraftingService->>ActivityRecorder: onQDocEvent(events)
  QDocDraftingService-->>QDocNotifier: after commit: QDocCreated, InvitationSent*
```
